title: OmniEvolve Phase 1: LJ924 and Occam’s Circuit
lede: The pipeline worked, but Phase 1 did not produce a competitive breakthrough: Occam reached a 399-gate exact solution, while LJ924 never beat its incumbent.

sections.title: Challenge
sections.note: What was attempted and what counts as success.

blocks.text: Phase 1 tested whether LLM-guided program evolution could solve two very different optimization challenges in one reusable framework. LJ924 asks for a lower-energy 924-atom Lennard–Jones cluster with strict force convergence. Occam’s Circuit asks for exact hidden Boolean functions using as few gates as possible.

Both tasks have hard, independent verification and an unambiguous ordering of valid solutions. A successful campaign would therefore demonstrate genuine algorithm discovery rather than subjective LLM code quality.

blocks.text: The evaluator was strengthened during the day. Occam failures gained first-counterexample and bit-level feedback. LJ separated the safe incumbent submission from the best exploratory proposal, so failed searches could no longer hide behind an unchanged fallback structure. These changes made the search observable, but did not create a competitive improvement.

sections.title: Results
sections.note: Competition value is separated from engineering value.

items.caption: Phase 1 outcome. Occam improved its earlier audited 422-gate implementation to a 399-gate exact solution, but the final restart did not beat 399. The 397-gate candidate is shown separately because it fails one output bit. LJ generated diverse proposals but recorded zero strict incumbent improvements.

blocks.label: Partial result, no final-restart gain
blocks.why: The broader day improved 422 → 399 exact gates, but the final 20-candidate restart found no exact candidate below 399.

rows: Average bit accuracy 0.9969618; one wrong bit on mystery-C
The loop explored distinct behaviors, not only source no-ops

blocks.label: No competitive improvement
blocks.why: No candidate achieved a strict energy improvement with the required force convergence; every valid submission retained the incumbent.

rows: Relocation, shrink and strain families were attempted
Exploration never cleared the strict gate

items: Occam has an exactness cliff: global natural-language rewrites often save gates by breaking a rare truth-table case. The missing primitive is formal local synthesis or equivalence-preserving peephole search.

LJ starts from an exceptionally well-relaxed incumbent. Single-core local perturbations usually return to the same basin or retain excessive force, while meaningful basin crossing needs a different search algorithm and much more parallel compute.
Failure memory and dense feedback improved diagnosis, but feedback cannot compensate for a candidate representation that does not expose safe, composable improvements.

sections.title: Highlight and Next Phase
sections.note: What is retained, what is archived, and why #229 is next.

blocks.text: Phase 1 produced an auditable evolution stack: behavioral counterexamples, proposal-versus-incumbent separation, durable failure memory, cross-provider fallback and content-addressed candidate history. These are infrastructure results, not substitutes for a winning solution.

Archive both brute-force campaigns. Preserve the Occam generation-15 397-gate candidate as a one-counterexample repair lead, but do not spend additional LLM generations on either task without changing the search representation.

Automated symmetry reduction for noncommutative moment hierarchies is a better OmniEvolve target because each mutation can be checked for exact or solver-tolerance equivalence, while block-size reduction and runtime provide continuous progress.

rows: Z₂ parity first; small permutation groups second
Dense and reduced SDP optima agree; reconstruction residual passes
Valid-equivalence tier, then block-size reduction and runtime
Only expand corpus after the small verifier suite is stable

blocks.label: Bottom line
blocks.text: The day was not a competitive success. Its useful conclusion is narrower and actionable: OmniEvolve needs verifier-bounded, composable candidate transformations. Issue #229 naturally supplies that structure; LJ924 does not, and Occam requires a formal synthesis backend before more evolution is justified.
